extracted.intended_audience: patent examiners and patent practitioners (applicants, prosecutors)
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and examiner guidance from the MPEP on how and when material may be incorporated by reference into U.S. patent applications, how to correct improper incorporations, related procedural requirements, and related rules on substitute (rewritten) specifications and prophetic examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.57(a) — inadvertent omission safeguard
rubrics_metrics.description: If a portion of the specification or drawings was inadvertently omitted, incorporation by reference is allowed where (a) the application contains a claim under § 1.55 or § 1.78 for priority/benefit present on the filing date, and (b) the omitted portion is completely contained in the prior-filed application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The application must be amended to include the omitted portion within any Office-set time period but no later than the close of prosecution (§ 1.114(b)) or abandonment. Applicant must supply a copy of the prior-filed application (except where the prior-filed application is filed under 35 U.S.C. 111), an English translation if needed, and identify where the omitted portion is found in the prior-filed application. Amendments to international applications under this paragraph are effective only as to the U.S. and do not affect international filing date; where no filing date is otherwise present, amendment must be by petition with fee (§ 1.17(f)).

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.57(b) — explicit wording and identification required
rubrics_metrics.description: An incorporation by reference (except as provided in § 1.57(a)) must appear in the specification and (1) express a clear intent to incorporate by reference using the root words 'incorporat(e)' and 'reference', and (2) clearly identify the referenced patent, application, or publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A mere reference to another document is not an incorporation; the Office treats references lacking the required root words as noncompliant and may require correction under § 1.57(g). Examiners will proceed as if no incorporation was made if the statement does not clearly convey intent, and will not expend resources to guess intent. Particular attention should be given to identifying specific portions of the referenced document where the incorporated subject matter is found.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'essential material' (37 CFR 1.57(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Essential material' is material necessary to: (1) provide a written description of the claimed invention and enable one skilled in the art to make and use it and set forth the best mode (35 U.S.C. 112, first paragraph); (2) describe the claimed invention in terms that particularly point out and distinctly claim it (35 U.S.C. 112, second paragraph); or (3) describe structure, material, or acts corresponding to a claimed means or step for performing a specified function (35 U.S.C. 112, sixth paragraph).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In applications that are to issue as U.S. patents, essential material may only be incorporated by reference to a U.S. patent or U.S. patent application publication that itself does not incorporate such essential material. Incorporation of essential material to unpublished U.S. applications, foreign applications/patents, or publications is improper under § 1.57(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted incorporation of nonessential material (37 CFR 1.57(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Nonessential material may be incorporated by reference to U.S. patents, U.S. patent application publications, foreign patents, foreign published applications, prior and concurrently filed commonly owned U.S. applications, or non-patent publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An incorporation by reference by hyperlink or other browser-executable code is not permitted. The Office policy aims to minimize public burden in locating incorporated material for patents that will issue; nonessential background/state-of-the-art matter is usually treated as nonessential and may be incorporated from various sources listed above.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner may require copies of incorporated material (37 CFR 1.57(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner may require the applicant to supply a copy of the material incorporated by reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If required, the supplied copy must be accompanied by a statement that it consists of the same material incorporated by reference in the referencing application. A copy may be required so the examiner can review what is being incorporated and place the material in context, or to verify that material inserted by amendment matches what was previously incorporated by reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Insertion of incorporated material via amendment (37 CFR 1.57(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: Any insertion of material originally incorporated by reference into the specification or drawings must be made by amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such an amendment must be accompanied by a statement that the material being inserted is the material previously incorporated by reference and that the amendment contains no new matter. Inserting material that was not originally incorporated by reference may introduce new matter and is restricted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of noncompliant incorporations and time limits (37 CFR 1.57(g))
rubrics_metrics.description: An incorporation that does not comply with § 1.57(b), (c), or (d) is ineffective to incorporate the material unless corrected within any time period set by the Office, but no later than the close of prosecution (§ 1.114(b)) or abandonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corrections permitted include adding the root words 'incorporate'/'reference' only if the application as filed clearly conveyed intent; corrections to identify a referenced document are permitted only if the document was sufficiently described to uniquely identify it. A correction that cannot identify the intended incorporated document may be new matter and is not authorized. Petition to suspend § 1.57(g) timing (37 CFR 1.183) is inappropriate; if abandoned, applicant must file a petition to revive (1.137); after issuance, correction must be via reissue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of improper incorporations during examination (procedural consequence)
rubrics_metrics.description: If incorporation by reference is improper (e.g., essential material incorporated from a foreign patent/publication or to an unpublished application), the incorporation is ineffective and the examiner should make the appropriate objection or rejection (for example under 35 U.S.C. 112) until applicant corrects it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must timely correct improper incorporations (within the period set in § 1.57(g)). Correction usually requires an amendment that inserts the material and the § 1.57(f) statement that no new matter is included. Failure to correct can result in rejections and may require after-final practice (§ 1.116), RCE (§ 1.114), filing a reissue after grant, or revival procedures if abandoned. Certificate of correction is not appropriate to fix incorporation-by-reference issues that would impact claim scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mere reference is not incorporation
rubrics_metrics.description: A mere reference to another application, patent, or publication does not incorporate anything therein for the disclosure required by 35 U.S.C. 112, first paragraph.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.57(b)(1) limits a proper incorporation to instances using the root words 'incorporate' and 'reference' (except for § 1.57(a) inadvertent omissions). If the required wording is absent, the Office will treat the reference as noncompliant and may require correction; exam will proceed as if no incorporation exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director's discretion and policy rationale
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director has considerable discretion in determining what may be incorporated by reference in a patent application; the Office's policy balances applicant convenience and the public's ability to find material in issued patents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy aims to ensure reasonably complete disclosures are published as U.S. patents so the public's burden to search for incorporated material is minimized. The Director codified practices in 37 CFR 1.57(b)-(g) (effective Oct 21, 2004) with changes for 18-month publication of applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporation practice for applications to issue as patents (limitations)
rubrics_metrics.description: For applications that will issue as U.S. patents, essential material may only be incorporated by reference to a U.S. patent or U.S. patent application publication (which itself does not incorporate essential material).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prior to Oct 21, 2004, incorporation to a pending U.S. application was permitted; that practice was discontinued. Nonessential material has broader incorporation options (see § 1.57(d)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporation practice for benefit/priority (earlier effective filing date) applications
rubrics_metrics.description: The limitations applicable to applications to issue as patents do not apply to earlier applications relied on solely to establish an earlier effective filing date under 35 U.S.C. 119 or 120.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An application may be entitled to rely on the filing date of an earlier application even if that earlier application incorporates essential material by reference. However, when benefit is claimed the applicant or patent owner may be required to supply copies (and translations) of material incorporated by reference so the Office can determine whether the earlier application discloses the invention as required by 35 U.S.C. 112.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples of corrective actions in response to examiner objections
rubrics_metrics.description: When an examiner finds that essential material was improperly incorporated (e.g., from a foreign patent), the examiner can require amendment to include the essential material within the reply period to a non-final Office action; failure to do so may justify a 35 U.S.C. 112 rejection in a final action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant later files an amendment to add the incorporated material, it must include the § 1.57(f) statement and may be filed as an after-final amendment (§ 1.116) or via RCE (§ 1.114) as appropriate. If applicant's claim amendment itself causes essentiality to arise, the examiner's rejection in a final action is proper and correction must follow post-final routes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simulated/predicted test results and prophetical (paper) examples
rubrics_metrics.description: Simulated or predicted test results and prophetic (paper) examples are permitted in patent applications, but must not be represented as work actually performed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Working examples correspond to work actually performed and may describe conducted tests and achieved results. Paper examples describe making an embodiment not actually performed; they should not be represented as actual results, should not be described using past tense, and no results should be claimed as actual unless they were actually achieved (see Hoffman-La Roche v. Promega).

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.125(a)-(c) — substitute (rewritten) specification required by Office
rubrics_metrics.description: If amendments or poor legibility make the application difficult to consider or to arrange papers for printing/copying, the Office may require the entire specification (including claims) or any part thereof be rewritten.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A substitute specification required by the Office under § 1.125(a) must be submitted with markings showing changes relative to the immediate prior version: underline added text; strike-through deleted text (or double brackets for small deletions); an accompanying clean version without markings must be supplied. A statement that the substitute specification contains no new matter must also be supplied. Numbering paragraphs of the specification of record is not considered a change requiring marking.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.125(b) — voluntary substitute specification
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject to § 1.312, an applicant may voluntarily file a substitute specification (excluding claims) at any point up to payment of the issue fee if accompanied by a statement that it includes no new matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Voluntary substitute specifications must also comply with the marking and clean-copy requirements noted in § 1.125(c). The Office will accept a voluntary substitute if § 1.125(b) requirements are satisfied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and style requirements for substitute specifications (idiomatic English)
rubrics_metrics.description: A substitute specification in proper idiomatic English and in compliance with 37 CFR 1.52(a) and (b) is required where the specification's English is faulty or otherwise deficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner may require a substitute specification for faulty English; use form paragraphs such as ¶ 6.28 and ¶ 6.28.01. A substitute specification is not permitted in a reissue application or in a reexamination proceeding.
